title: Tech Note: Cleaning Whitespace from XML Values
author: David Adams
featured_technology: DOM XML commands (DOM GET XML ELEMENT VALUE)
SAX XML commands (SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE)

historical_commentary.text: This note addresses a real gap in 4D 2004's built-in XML commands, which returned element values including leading/trailing whitespace exactly as the XML spec requires but developers often didn't want. The array-driven trimming technique it teaches is a solid general programming pattern that remains conceptually valid, but the specific DOM/SAX commands referenced are legacy 4D language APIs from a pre-ORDA, pre-Project-Mode era. Modern 4D code would more likely use built-in string trim functions or newer XML/JSON handling rather than hand-rolled whitespace scanning.
related_updates: 4D has since added native string trimming capabilities and expanded XML/JSON parsing commands in later versions
The DOM/SAX XML command set discussed here still exists in modern 4D but is increasingly superseded by JSON-based data exchange in contemporary 4D development
